content.title: About
content.content: Rob Roy is a classic cocktail made with Scotch whisky, sweet vermouth, and Angostura bitters. It was created in the early 1900s in New York, inspired by the popular operetta “Rob Roy.” The drink is known for its smooth, slightly sweet and spicy flavor with a hint of bitterness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first Rob Roy recipe appeared in the 1900s at the Waldorf Astoria bar in New York.
The cocktail is named after the Scottish poet Robert “Rob” Roy MacGregor, known as Rob Roy.
There are several variations: Sweet Rob Roy (with red vermouth), Dry Rob Roy (with dry vermouth) and Perfect Rob Roy (half sweet, half dry vermouth).
Angostura bitters, used in the recipe, were created in the 1850s in Barbados and remain one of the most popular cocktail bitters.
Rob Roy is traditionally served in a cocktail glass, though a martinez glass is sometimes used for a more refined presentation.

items.title: Moderate consumption may promote relaxation
items.content: A small amount of whisky can have a calming effect due to the alcohol’s mild sedative properties.

items.title: Contains antioxidants from vermouth
items.content: Both sweet and dry vermouth are wine‑based and contain polyphenols that act as antioxidants.

items.title: Angostura bitters provide aromatic herbs
items.content: Bitters often include extracts of bitter herbs traditionally used in herbal medicine.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: The cocktail contains ethanol, so it should be consumed responsibly and avoided during pregnancy, driving, or liver disease.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweet vermouth adds sugar, which may be unsuitable for people with diabetes or low‑carb diets.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to the herbal components in Angostura bitters.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Combine 45 ml Scotch whisky, 20 ml sweet or dry vermouth, and a few dashes of Angostura bitters in a mixing glass with ice. Stir, strain into a chilled cocktail glass, and garnish with a cherry or an orange twist. Serve neat, without ice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Alcoholic ingredients (whisky, vermouth, bitters) should be kept in tightly sealed bottles in a cool, dark place. Once opened, vermouth is best stored in the refrigerator, while bitters can remain at room temperature away from direct light.
